# Pumpswap — Full Documentation

Product name: **Pumpswap**
Production website: **https://liquidpump.app**
Blockchain: **Solana** (on-chain Anchor program)

> This document describes the Pumpswap implementation as it exists in the
> current codebase. It documents what is implemented, not a roadmap. Where a
> capability is planned but not implemented, or deployed only to Devnet and not
> yet to Mainnet, that is stated explicitly.

Naming and branding: the product is called **Pumpswap**. The production website
domain is **liquidpump.app**. These refer to the same product; "liquidpump.app"
is the production domain, not a separate brand. Pumpswap is an independent
Solana staking platform and is **not** a Pump.fun affiliate or product, and is
not affiliated with Pump.fun in any way.

---

## A. PROJECT OVERVIEW

### What Pumpswap is

Pumpswap is a no-code Solana staking platform. It lets a Solana project team
create, fund, and manage a token staking pool through a web console, and then
share a ready-made, brandable staking portal with its community. The staking,
reward accrual, and reward-claim logic runs in an on-chain Anchor program
(`pumpswap_staking`); the web application is a client that builds and submits
transactions to that program.

### Who it serves and the problems it solves

Pumpswap is designed for **Solana project founders and token teams**. Building
token staking normally requires designing and deploying a custom smart
contract, writing a front end, and handling reward accounting. Pumpswap removes
most of that work: a founder configures a pool, funds a reward vault, and gets
a staking portal. Stakers connect their own Solana wallet, stake tokens, watch
rewards accrue, and claim — all against the on-chain program.

### Relationship between the Pumpswap product name and the liquidpump.app domain

"Pumpswap" is the product name. "https://liquidpump.app" is the production
website domain for that same product. They are not two different products. All
production links in this documentation use https://liquidpump.app.

### The Solana staking use case

A founder chooses a staking token (the token users lock) and a reward token
(the token distributed to stakers), sets a lock-up duration and an initial
reward emission rate, and deploys the pool on-chain. The founder then funds the

---

## B. PLATFORM ARCHITECTURE

Pumpswap has three layers: a Next.js web client, an on-chain Anchor program,
and wallet integration for signing transactions.

### Frontend

The web application is a Next.js (App Router) React application. It reads
on-chain state through a read-only Anchor client and submits transactions
through a wallet-backed Anchor client (`lib/solana/program.ts`). Key modules:

- `lib/solana/connection.ts` — builds the Solana `Connection`. Browser RPC
  calls go through a same-origin proxy (`/api/rpc`) so no credentialed RPC URL
  reaches the browser.
- `lib/solana/network.ts` — resolves the configured cluster and RPC endpoints.
- `lib/solana/ops.ts` — typed helpers that build each program instruction
  (createPool, stake, unstake, claim, fund rewards, pause, freeze, set boost,
  set reward rate) and fetch pool / position accounts.
- `lib/solana/pda.ts` — derives all program PDAs (see "Pool accounts" below).
- `lib/solana/token.ts` — detects whether a mint is owned by the classic SPL
  Token program or Token-2022 and reads it with the correct program.
- `lib/solana/rewards-calc.ts` — pure, dependency-free reward/APR math.

### Solana program

The on-chain program is `pumpswap_staking`, an Anchor program
(`programs/pumpswap-staking/src/lib.rs`). Its instructions are:
`initialize_platform`, `create_pool`, `set_pool_boost`, `fund_rewards`,
`stake`, `unstake`, `claim_rewards`, `pause_pool`, `emergency_freeze`, and
`set_reward_rate`.

Reward accounting uses a `reward_per_token` accumulator scaled by
`REWARD_SCALE = 1_000_000_000_000_000_000` (1e18). On each state-changing
action, `update_pool_rewards` advances the accumulator by
`elapsed * reward_rate_per_second * REWARD_SCALE / total_staked`. When
`total_staked == 0`, time passes but nothing accrues. Each user position stores
a `reward_debt` snapshot so a user's newly accrued rewards are the delta since
their last settle.

### Wallet integration

Wallet connection uses `@solana/wallet-adapter-react`. The wallets configured
in the codebase are **Phantom** and **Solflare**
(`components/solana/solana-providers.tsx`). Users authorize every transaction
with their own wallet; Pumpswap never signs on a user's behalf.

### Pool accounts and reward vaults (PDAs)

All program accounts are PDAs derived from the program ID. The seeds are:

- `platform`: `["platform"]` — one-time platform config (admin, fee_bps).
- `pool`: `["pool", authority, pool_id_le_bytes]`
- `staking_vault`: `["staking_vault", pool]`
- `reward_vault`: `["reward_vault", pool]`
- `user_position`: `["user_position", pool, user]`

The `staking_vault` and `reward_vault` are SPL/Token-2022 token accounts whose
**authority is the pool PDA** (the program signs for them via PDA seeds). This
is what makes the design non-custodial.

### Non-custodial design (as supported by the implementation)

- Staked tokens are transferred from the user into the pool's `staking_vault`,
  a token account owned by the pool PDA. They are never held by Pumpswap.
- Reward tokens are transferred from a funder into the pool's `reward_vault`,
  also owned by the pool PDA.
- On `unstake`, the program signs (via the pool PDA seeds) to return staking
  tokens from the vault to the user's token account.
- On `claim_rewards`, the program signs (via the pool PDA seeds) to transfer
  accrued rewards from the reward vault to the user's reward token account.
- There is **no instruction that lets a pool authority or platform admin
  withdraw a staker's deposited tokens**. The authority can pause, freeze,
  change the reward rate, and configure an NFT boost — but cannot extract user
  principal from the staking vault.

### Responsibilities of pool authorities and stakers

- **Pool authority** (the wallet that created the pool): funds the reward
  vault; sets the reward rate (Target APR or direct); configures the NFT boost;
  can pause, emergency-freeze, and restore the pool.
- **Staker** (any user): stakes, unstakes after the lock period, and claims
  accrued rewards. The staker signs their own transactions from their own
  wallet.

pool's reward vault with reward tokens. Users stake the staking token; rewards
accrue over time based on the pool's emission rate and each user's share of the
total stake; users unstake (after any lock period) and claim rewards.

---

## C. STAKING POOLS

### Pool creation and management

A pool is created with the `create_pool` instruction, which takes:

- `pool_id: u64` — a founder-chosen identifier (part of the pool PDA seeds, so a
  single authority can operate multiple distinct pools).
- `lock_duration: i64` — seconds tokens stay locked (must be `>= 0`; `0` means
  "flexible" / no lock).
- `reward_rate_per_second: u64` — the initial emission rate in reward-token
  base units per second (must be `> 0`).

Creation also initializes the `staking_vault` and `reward_vault` token accounts
and stores the staking mint, reward mint, and their bumps on the pool account.
In the console, the Create Pool wizard (`/create-pool`) walks through pool
details, reward configuration, and review, then submits `create_pool` (and, if
an NFT boost is configured, `set_pool_boost`).

### Staking

The `stake` instruction:

- Requires `amount > 0`.
- Reverts if the pool is paused or emergency-frozen.
- Transfers `amount` of the staking token from the user into the staking
  vault.
- Increments the user position's `amount` and the pool's `total_staked`.
- Sets the position's `locked_until` to `now + lock_duration` (it only ever
  moves forward, so a new stake extends the lock rather than shortening it).
- Settles the user's accrued rewards up to the current accumulator value.
- If NFT boost is enabled on the pool, verifies and records the boost (see
  section G).

### Withdrawing (unstaking)

The `unstake` instruction:

- Requires the caller to own the position and `amount > 0`.
- Requires the position to hold at least `amount`.
- Requires `now >= locked_until` (the lock period must be met); otherwise it
  reverts with `LockDurationNotMet`.
- Settles accrued rewards, reduces the position and pool totals, and returns
  `amount` of staking tokens from the vault to the user.

### Claiming rewards

The `claim_rewards` instruction:

- Requires the caller to own the position.
- Settles rewards, then requires `total_rewards > 0` (`NoRewardsToClaim`).
- Requires the reward vault to hold at least `total_rewards`
  (`InsufficientRewardVaultBalance`).
- Zeroes the position's `accrued_rewards`, adds to `total_claimed`, and
  transfers the reward tokens from the vault to the user's reward token
  account.

### Lock-up rules

The lock duration is set at pool creation and stored on-chain. It cannot be
changed after deployment. Each stake sets (or extends) `locked_until`. A
`lock_duration` of `0` yields "flexible" staking with no lock. Unstaking before
`locked_until` is not permitted.

### Multiple pools operate independently

Each pool is its own PDA with its own vaults, mints, lock duration, emission
rate, pause/freeze flags, and NFT-boost configuration. One authority can run
many pools (distinguished by `pool_id`). Pools do not share reward vaults or
accrual state.

### Pool-authority restrictions

The following are **authority-only** (the signing wallet must equal
`pool.authority`, enforced on-chain): `set_pool_boost`, `pause_pool`,
`emergency_freeze`, and `set_reward_rate`. `fund_rewards` can be called by any
funder who holds reward tokens; it is not restricted to the authority. Staking,
unstaking, and claiming are open to any user wallet, subject to the pool's
pause/freeze state and lock rules.


---

## D. REWARD FUNDING AND EMISSIONS

### Depositing reward tokens

`fund_rewards(amount)` transfers `amount` of the reward token from the funder's
token account into the pool's `reward_vault` (via `transfer_checked`, using the
reward mint's on-chain decimals). Any wallet holding the reward token can fund
the vault; funding is not limited to the pool authority.

### Configuring reward emissions

The pool stores a single `reward_rate_per_second` (reward-token base units per
second). Emissions are changed with the `set_reward_rate` instruction, which is
authority-only. The console's Reward Settings card (`/admin`) exposes two
equivalent ways to choose the rate:

- **Target APR mode** — the owner states a target APR and a reference
  (expected) staking amount. The app derives the per-second emission with
  `emissionPerSecondForTargetApr` (see section E). This mode is only offered
  when the staking token and reward token are the **same mint** (one shared
  valuation), because converting an APR into an emission requires comparing
  like-for-like value.
- **Direct Reward Rate mode** — the owner states the emission directly in
  reward tokens per day. No APR is claimed, so this mode works for every pool,
  including cross-token pools.

Both modes produce the same on-chain value (`reward_rate_per_second`) and are
submitted through `setRewardRate()`.

### How changing the reward rate affects future rewards

`set_reward_rate` is deliberately ordered to be safe for already-accrued
rewards:

1. It first calls `update_pool_rewards`, settling `reward_per_token` up to the
   current time at the **current (old) rate**. All rewards accrued before the
   change keep their original terms — nothing is recalculated retroactively.
2. Only then does it store the new `reward_rate_per_second`.

The instruction moves no tokens. Rewards accrued after the change accrue at the
new rate.

### Reward-vault balance limits payouts

The program never creates reward tokens; it only distributes what is in the
`reward_vault`. `claim_rewards` reverts with `InsufficientRewardVaultBalance`
when the vault cannot cover the user's accrued total. A pool that runs out of
funded rewards simply stops paying out until the vault is funded again. Accrued
but unclaimed rewards remain recorded on the position.

### Reward-budget duration estimates

The client provides budget planning helpers (in `lib/solana/rewards-calc.ts`):

- `requiredRewardBudgetBase(emission, duration) = emission * duration` — how
  much must be funded for the emission to run for a chosen duration.
- `fundingSustainSeconds(budget, emission) = budget / emission` — how long a
  funded budget lasts at the current emission (whole seconds, floored).
- `validateRewardFunding(...)` — reports whether a chosen budget covers a chosen
  duration and any shortfall.

These are planning estimates based on a constant-emission assumption.

### What an emission rate is (and is not)

An emission rate is a **distribution rate**, not a guaranteed return. It
describes how many reward tokens are distributed per second across all stakers.
It does not guarantee that any individual staker receives a particular return,
and funding a reward vault does not automatically guarantee any APR. Realized
returns depend on total stake, how long a user stakes, and the reward vault
staying funded.


---

## E. APR CALCULATIONS

### Non-compounding APR estimate

All APR figures in Pumpswap are **non-compounding annual percentage rate
(APR) estimates**, never APY. The on-chain program does not auto-compound
rewards. The core estimate (`estimatedAprBps`) is:

```
estimated APR = (emissionPerSecond * SECONDS_PER_YEAR * 10_000) / totalStaked
```

computed in exact integer math, using `SECONDS_PER_YEAR = 31_536_000`
(365 days).

### Realized APR changes as total stake changes

The emission rate is fixed until the owner changes it, but APR is inversely
proportional to total stake. As more users stake, the same emission is spread
across a larger base, so each staker's share — and the estimated APR — goes
down. Conversely, if stake decreases, the estimated APR rises. The displayed
estimate reflects the pool's **current** on-chain total stake.

### Target APR reference-stake input

In Target APR mode the owner enters a **reference stake** — the amount of
staking token the owner expects to be staked. The emission is sized so that,
*if* total stake equals that reference amount, the realized APR matches the
target. If actual stake differs from the reference, the realized APR will
differ from the target. The reference stake is an assumption, not a guarantee.

### Why same-mint pools can have a calculable APR

When the staking token and the reward token are the **same mint**, both sides of
the ratio are the same unit of value, and the mint decimals are known from the
chain. The reward emission and the total stake can then be compared directly
after a decimals adjustment, so a meaningful APR can be computed.

### Why cross-token pools cannot reliably display APR

When the staking token and reward token are different mints, comparing them
requires a price conversion (how many reward tokens one staking token is
worth). Pumpswap has **no price feed and no price-conversion mechanism**
(by design — see the notes in `lib/solana/rewards-calc.ts`). Without a price,
a cross-token APR would be meaningless, so these pools are treated as
"APR not computable" rather than showing a misleading number. Owners of
cross-token pools use Direct Reward Rate mode.

### Why unknown decimals, zero stake, or zero emission prevent APR

The APR math returns "not available" (not a guess) when it cannot be computed:

- **Unknown mint decimals** — if the exact decimals cannot be read from the mint
  account, the token-unit conversion is unknown, so APR cannot be computed.
- **Zero stake** — with no stake, rewards accrue to nobody and the ratio is
  undefined.
- **Zero emission** — with no emission there is no reward to annualize.

### Dashboard "Average Estimated APR"

The dashboard's Average Estimated APR (`computeAverageEstimatedApr`) is the
**arithmetic mean of the current estimated APR of every eligible pool**. A pool
is eligible only when all of the following hold:

- The staking and reward tokens are the **same mint** (cross-token pools are
  excluded — no price feed).
- Both mint decimals are known (read from chain).
- There is stake (`totalStaked > 0`) and there is an emission
  (`emissionPerSecond > 0`).

Pools that fail any of these are excluded, and the dashboard reports how many
pools were included and the reason each excluded pool was dropped
(cross-token, unknown decimals, no stake yet, or no emission). The Target APR
reference/preview value is **not** used in this average.

### The average is an estimate, not a promised return

The Average Estimated APR is a non-compounding estimate based on current on-
chain emission and current stake. It is not a promised, guaranteed, or
risk-free return, and it is not APY.


---

## F. TOKEN COMPATIBILITY

### Supported token programs

The program's token accounts are declared with Anchor's `token_interface`
(`InterfaceAccount<Mint>`, `InterfaceAccount<TokenAccount>`, and
`Interface<TokenInterface>`), and all transfers use `transfer_checked` with the
mint's on-chain decimals. This means each pool may use, for its staking mint
and/or its reward mint, either:

- the **original SPL Token program** (`TOKEN_PROGRAM_ID`), or
- **Token-2022** (`TOKEN_2022_PROGRAM_ID`).

The client (`lib/solana/token.ts`) reads the mint account and detects which
program owns it, then unpacks it with the correct program — a Token-2022 mint
is never read through the legacy program.

### Known limitations (stated accurately)

- Support covers the standard mint/transfer behavior that `token_interface`
  provides. Pumpswap does **not** implement special handling for individual
  Token-2022 extensions (for example, transfer fees/hooks, confidential
  transfers, or interest-bearing logic). Do not assume that a mint is fully
  compatible merely because it uses Token-2022: a mint whose extension behavior
  interferes with `transfer_checked` or vault accounting may not work as
  expected.
- Not every Token-2022 extension is supported. Compatibility has been exercised
  for the standard transfer path on both classic SPL and Token-2022 mints; it
  has not been verified for every extension configuration.


---

## G. NFT STAKING BOOSTS

### What is implemented

A pool authority can enable an NFT boost with `set_pool_boost(collection,
boost_bps)`:

- `boost_bps` is in basis points, capped at `MAX_NFT_BOOST_BPS = 10_000`
  (i.e., up to +100% extra rewards).
- A positive boost requires a non-default `collection` address; a `boost_bps`
  of `0` clears and disables the boost (enforced both on-chain by
  `normalize_boost` and in the client).

### How boost eligibility is checked and applied

When a pool has an NFT boost enabled, the `stake` instruction requires two
additional accounts — the user's NFT token account and the NFT's Metaplex
metadata account — and verifies on-chain that:

- The NFT token account is owned by the staking user and holds at least one
  token.
- The metadata account is the canonical Metaplex metadata PDA for the NFT mint
  and describes that same mint.
- The metadata has a collection, that collection is **verified** by the
  Metaplex authority, and it **matches** the pool's configured collection.

If any check fails, the stake reverts. When boost is not enabled, these NFT
accounts are optional and ordinary staking works without them.

### How the boost value is applied (and snapshotted)

The boost applied to a position always comes from the **pool configuration**,
never from anything the frontend supplies. At stake time the program writes the
pool's `nft_boost_bps` onto the user's `UserPosition` (`nft_boost_bps`). This
value is **snapshotted on the position at staking time**. Reward accrual then
applies the boost to the newly settled portion only:

```
boosted = baseReward * (10_000 + nftBoostBps) / 10_000
```

Already-accrued rewards are not re-boosted. If the pool's boost is later
changed, existing positions keep the boost value recorded when they staked.

### Collection verification requirement

Only NFTs from the pool's configured collection, with a Metaplex-verified
collection, satisfy the boost. Not every NFT collection is supported
automatically — the collection must be explicitly configured on the pool and
verified on-chain.


---

## H. ADMINISTRATION AND SECURITY

### Pool-authority authorization

Authority-gated instructions (`set_pool_boost`, `pause_pool`,
`emergency_freeze`, `set_reward_rate`) enforce, on-chain, that the signing
wallet equals `pool.authority`. A non-authority wallet cannot execute them.

### Pause and emergency freeze

Two independent boolean flags on the pool control availability:

- **Pause** (`pause_pool`, authority-only): when paused, new `stake` deposits
  revert with `PoolPaused`.
- **Emergency freeze** (`emergency_freeze`, authority-only): when frozen, new
  `stake` deposits revert with `PoolFrozen`, and `set_reward_rate` also reverts
  with `PoolFrozen` (a frozen pool accepts no emission changes).

Both are reversible by the authority (pause on/off, freeze on/off).

### What the controls affect (per the actual instruction constraints)

- `pause` and `emergency_freeze` **only block new staking deposits**. They do
  **not** block `unstake` or `claim_rewards` — the `unstake` and
  `claim_rewards` instructions do not check the `paused`/`frozen` flags. This
  means users can always withdraw their staked tokens (after the lock period)
  and claim already-accrued rewards, even while a pool is paused or frozen.
- `emergency_freeze` additionally blocks `set_reward_rate`; `pause` does not.
- `fund_rewards` is not blocked by pause or freeze.

### How users authorize transactions

Users sign every transaction with their own wallet (Phantom or Solflare)
through the Solana wallet adapter. The program verifies account ownership and
PDA constraints on-chain. Pumpswap never holds, generates, or controls users'
private keys.

### Account validation and reward-vault protections

- Mint constraints verify the supplied staking/reward mints match the pool's
  configured mints (`InvalidMint`).
- Token-account constraints verify the mint, authority (user or pool), and
  token program, and vaults are validated against their PDA seeds and stored
  bumps.
- Reward claims are capped by the actual `reward_vault` balance
  (`InsufficientRewardVaultBalance`), so the program cannot pay out more than
  the vault holds.
- Arithmetic uses checked math with overflow guards (`MathOverflow`).

### Security posture (stated accurately)

- **No professional third-party smart-contract audit is claimed.** Do not
  describe the contracts as audited.
- The platform is **not** claimed to be immune to vulnerabilities.
- **Devnet testing is not a security audit.** Activity on Devnet validates
  behavior but does not constitute a security review or a Mainnet readiness
  guarantee.


---

## I. WALLET AND NETWORK SUPPORT

### Configured network

The repository is configured for **Solana Devnet**. This is set by
`NEXT_PUBLIC_SOLANA_NETWORK=devnet` (in `.env.example` and the local
environment) and by `cluster = "devnet"` in `Anchor.toml`. The client supports
`devnet`, `testnet`, and `mainnet-beta` in code (`lib/solana/network.ts`), but
the deployed configuration in this repository is Devnet.

### Devnet vs. Mainnet

- Testing and the current deployment are on **Devnet**.
- **Mainnet support/availability is not established** in this repository. A
  feature that works on Devnet should not be assumed to be available or
  production-ready on Mainnet.

### Wallet support

Only wallets verified in the codebase are: **Phantom** and **Solflare**
(configured in `components/solana/solana-providers.tsx`). No other wallets are
explicitly configured, though the standard wallet-adapter modal is used.

---

## J. DEVELOPER INFORMATION

### Program architecture (high level)

- Language/framework: Rust + Anchor. The program module is `pumpswap_staking`.
- On-chain accounts: `Platform` (one-time config: `admin`, `fee_bps`, `bump`),
  `Pool` (authority, pool_id, staking/reward mints, vault addresses,
  lock_duration, reward_rate_per_second, total_staked, reward_per_token,
  last_update_timestamp, paused, frozen, bumps, nft_collection, nft_boost_bps),
  and `UserPosition` (owner, pool, amount, locked_until, reward_debt,
  accrued_rewards, total_claimed, bump, nft_boost_bps).
- Instructions: `initialize_platform`, `create_pool`, `set_pool_boost`,
  `fund_rewards`, `stake`, `unstake`, `claim_rewards`, `pause_pool`,
  `emergency_freeze`, `set_reward_rate`.
- PDA seeds: `["platform"]`; `["pool", authority, pool_id_le]`;
  `["staking_vault", pool]`; `["reward_vault", pool]`;
  `["user_position", pool, user]`.

### Program ID

The deployed program ID is **`BYc1mF65g1JNr44BWefhnhKdPLDWbxcdUoKxcoDeZMWs`**.
It is declared in `programs/pumpswap-staking/src/lib.rs` (`declare_id!`), in
`Anchor.toml`, and in the IDL, and is read from
`NEXT_PUBLIC_STAKING_PROGRAM_ID` in the client. It is a public Devnet address
and is appropriate to publish.

### Client integration

The frontend uses `@coral-xyz/anchor` with the program IDL
(`lib/solana/idl/pumpswap_staking.json`) to build and send transactions, and to
fetch/deserialize `Pool` and `UserPosition` accounts. PDA derivation lives in
`lib/solana/pda.ts`; per-instruction builders live in `lib/solana/ops.ts`; the
shared reward/APR math lives in `lib/solana/rewards-calc.ts` (pure, no web3
dependency).

### What is NOT provided

There is **no** public SDK package, REST/GraphQL API, webhook service, or
indexer API implemented in this codebase. Developer integration is via the
on-chain Anchor program and its IDL. Do not invent SDK packages, API endpoints,
webhooks, or hosted developer services.

### Secrets and credentials

No private keys, seed phrases, passwords, RPC API secrets, or `.env` values are
published here. RPC access from the browser goes through a same-origin proxy;
server-side RPC credentials are never exposed to the client. This documentation
intentionally omits all environment credentials.

## K. FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

**What is Pumpswap?**
Pumpswap is a no-code Solana staking platform for project founders to create,
fund, and manage non-custodial token staking pools and share a staking portal,
backed by an on-chain Anchor program.

**Who is Pumpswap designed for?**
Solana project founders and token teams that want to offer staking to their
community without building a custom staking contract and front end.

**How does a project create a staking pool?**
Connect the founder wallet, open Create Pool, choose a staking token and a
reward token, set a lock duration and a reward rate (Target APR or Direct
Reward Rate), optionally configure an NFT boost, and submit. This runs
`create_pool` on-chain (and `set_pool_boost` if a boost is configured).

**How are rewards funded?**
By transferring reward tokens into the pool's reward vault with `fund_rewards`.
Any wallet holding the reward token can fund it. Claims are limited by the
vault balance, so the vault must stay funded for payouts to continue.

**Who can change a pool's reward rate?**
Only the pool authority (the wallet that created the pool), via the
authority-only `set_reward_rate` instruction. It is also blocked while the pool
is emergency-frozen.

**Does Target APR guarantee a return?**
No. Target APR is an owner-selected goal used to size the emission against a
reference stake. The realized APR depends on actual total stake and changes as
stake changes. It is a non-compounding estimate, not a guarantee or APY.

**Why might a pool show no APR?**
Because the APR cannot be reliably computed: the staking and reward tokens are
different mints (cross-token, no price feed), the mint decimals are unknown,
there is no stake yet, or there is no emission.

**Why can the dashboard exclude a pool from Average Estimated APR?**
The average uses only eligible pools. A pool is excluded when it is cross-token
(no price feed), has unknown decimals, has no stake yet, or has no emission.
The dashboard shows how many pools were included and why others were excluded.

**What happens when a reward vault has insufficient tokens?**
`claim_rewards` reverts with `InsufficientRewardVaultBalance`. Accrued rewards
remain recorded on the user's position and can be claimed after the vault is
funded again.

**Does Pumpswap support Token-2022?**
Yes — pools may use the original SPL Token program or Token-2022 for their
staking and/or reward mints (standard mint/transfer behavior via
`token_interface`). Not every Token-2022 extension is specially supported, so
compatibility depends on the specific mint's extension behavior.

**Is the current deployment on Devnet or Mainnet?**
Devnet. The repository is configured for Solana Devnet. Mainnet availability is
not established here.

**Does Pumpswap create or control users' private keys?**
No. Users connect their own wallet (Phantom or Solflare) and sign their own
transactions. Pumpswap never holds or controls private keys and cannot move a
user's funds.


---

## L. CURRENT LIMITATIONS AND AVAILABILITY

### Implemented and Devnet-tested functionality

The following are implemented in the current codebase and have been exercised
on Devnet:

- Pool creation and management (`create_pool`).
- Funding rewards (`fund_rewards`).
- Staking, unstaking (after lock), and claiming rewards (`stake`, `unstake`,
  `claim_rewards`).
- Owner-controlled reward-rate updates (`set_reward_rate`) and both Target APR
  and Direct Reward Rate configuration paths.
- NFT staking boosts (`set_pool_boost`) with on-chain collection verification.
- Pause and emergency-freeze controls (`pause_pool`, `emergency_freeze`).
- SPL Token and Token-2022 support for the standard mint/transfer path.
- Dashboards, analytics, and activity views.

### Important implementation limitations

- **APR is a non-compounding estimate, not APY**, and changes with total stake.
- **Cross-token pools cannot display a reliable APR** (no price feed).
- **Pools with unknown decimals, zero stake, or zero emission show no APR.**
- **Reward payouts are capped by the reward-vault balance.**
- **Pause/freeze block new stakes only**; unstaking and claiming remain
  available. `emergency_freeze` additionally blocks reward-rate changes.
- **Lock duration is fixed at creation** and cannot be changed.
- **NFT boost is snapshotted on the position at stake time.**
- **Token-2022 support covers standard mint/transfer behavior only**; not every
  extension is supported.
- The `set_reward_rate` instruction exists in the current program source, but
  the deployed program may predate it; the client probes the deployed program
  before offering the control (`isSetRewardRateSupported`).

### Devnet-tested vs. Mainnet availability

- Functionality above is **Devnet-tested**. The current deployment target is
  **Solana Devnet**.
- **Mainnet availability is not established** in this repository. Nothing here
  should be read as confirming that these features are deployed and verified on
  Mainnet.

### What is not claimed

- **No professional smart-contract audit** is claimed.
- **No guarantee** of returns, fixed profits, or risk-free staking.
- **No claim** of immunity to vulnerabilities; Devnet testing is not a security
  audit.
- **No specific claims** about uptime, TVL, user counts, partnerships,
  integrations, or adoption.
- Building successfully does **not** by itself make a feature Mainnet-ready.
